rungs.title: Free-space motion
rungs.description: Three minimum-jerk tool moves through free space, 0.8 s each with 0.3 s rests. Tests plain tracking with the feed-forward the trajectory carries.

gates.why: tracks a slow free-space path within a degree
the motion fits the boards' torque (at the cap < 2 % of the time)
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
no board fault and no controller abort
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
a command goes out within one host period (10 ms) of the sample it came from

rungs.title: Fast free-space motion
rungs.description: The same tool path at 0.3 s per move, near the boards' torque limits. Tests tracking when inertia, not gravity, dominates.

gates.why: tracks a fast free-space path within 3 degrees
the fast motion stays mostly inside the boards' torque
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
a command goes out within one host period (10 ms) of the sample it came from

rungs.title: Sideways push
rungs.description: The arm holds home while a 15 N push along +x acts on the tool for 0.4 s. Tests stiffness under a disturbance and how fast and cleanly it recovers.

gates.why: back within 1 mm of the pre-push pose within 0.5 s
springs back past the pose by no more than 5 mm
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
a command goes out within one host period (10 ms) of the sample it came from

rungs.title: Host stall
rungs.description: R1's path with 0.3 ms of wake jitter and one 0.5 s host stall at t = 0.8 s (the F09 hang); the boards' watchdog brakes the arm. Tests that the controller comes back on schedule.

gates.why: nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
ends on the input's schedule after the stall (a slipping clock fails)
settles within 1 s after the reference ends

rungs.title: Fast free-space motion with an unmodelled payload
rungs.description: R2's fast tool path with a 0.3 kg payload on the tool that no feed-forward model knows (the trajectory's effort column and every model are the nominal arm's). Tests how much of a model error feedback closes, and where it is closed.

gates.why: tracks a fast free-space path within 3 degrees
the fast motion stays mostly inside the boards' torque
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
a command goes out within one host period (10 ms) of the sample it came from

rungs.title: Fast free-space motion, host at 50 Hz
rungs.description: Rung R2 with the host loop at 50 Hz instead of 100 Hz. Tests how the host rate moves tracking for a law closed on the host vs on the board.

gates.why: tracks a fast free-space path within 3 degrees
the fast motion stays mostly inside the boards' torque
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
a command goes out within one host period (20 ms) of the sample it came from

rungs.title: Fast free-space motion, host at 500 Hz
rungs.description: Rung R2 with the host loop at 500 Hz instead of 100 Hz. Tests how the host rate moves tracking for a law closed on the host vs on the board.

gates.why: tracks a fast free-space path within 3 degrees
the fast motion stays mostly inside the boards' torque
nothing went non-finite or out of bounds
the host kept its rate: no period went by without a command
